main_text.head: MEDICARVM LIBER V. De Medendi Methodo.
CAP. I. De Indicatione.
main_text.p: CUm Medicina circa corpus ægrum maximè versetur, ut morbus nimirum profligetur, & natura conservetur; cognitis morbo, causa, locoque affecto, nihil superesse videtur aliud, quam medicamenti idonei & alimenti inventio. illo morbus corrumpitur, hoc facultas conservatur. Hoc fieri nequit, ignoratis iis, quæ secundum & præter naturam homini accidunt. Proinde Medicus, naturæ minister, nunquam huiusmodi scopos attinget, ignoratis iis, quę ante à nobis sunt dicta. Itaque Empirici,

page.notes: The left-hand page edge carries faint, mostly illegible marginal fragments (e.g. "lacca", "s", "quam", "scopos") that belong to the facing page and were not transcribed. The initial "C" is a large woodcut-style letter joined to "Um". The word "Medicina" and the first letters of the division heading are set in small capitals; "CAP. I." is set in small capitals. The chapter heading "De Indicatione" is italic.
